q: Chemistry is an area of knowledge remarkable for its breadth and ____.
e: Chemistry is an area of knowledge remarkable for its breadth and depth. Depth is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Knowledge of chemistry is essential to improve the quality of our ____.
e: Knowledge of chemistry is essential to improve the quality of our lives. Lives is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Faster electronic devices, stronger plastics, and more effective medicines and vaccines all rely on the innovations of ____ throughout the world.
e: Faster electronic devices, stronger plastics, and more effective medicines and vaccines all rely on the innovations of chemists throughout the world. Chemists is the idea that completes this fact.

q: We cannot truly understand or even know very much about the world we live in or about our own bodies without knowing the fundamental concepts of ____.
e: We cannot truly understand or even know very much about the world we live in or about our own bodies without knowing the fundamental concepts of chemistry. Chemistry is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____, water contamination, air pollution, food shortages and other societal issues are regularly featured in the media.
e: Climate change, water contamination, air pollution, food shortages and other societal issues are regularly featured in the media. Climate change is a long-term shift in weather patterns, driven strongly by greenhouse gases. Chemistry of greenhouse gases is a main tool for understanding climate change.

q: Climate change, ____, air pollution, food shortages and other societal issues are regularly featured in the media.
e: Climate change, water contamination, air pollution, food shortages and other societal issues are regularly featured in the media. Water contamination is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Climate change, water contamination, ____, food shortages and other societal issues are regularly featured in the media.
e: Climate change, water contamination, air pollution, food shortages and other societal issues are regularly featured in the media. Air pollution is a high level of harmful gases or particles in the air.

q: Climate change, water contamination, air pollution, ____ and other societal issues are regularly featured in the media.
e: Climate change, water contamination, air pollution, food shortages and other societal issues are regularly featured in the media. Food shortages is the idea that completes this fact.

q: As the '____', chemistry is woven into the fabric of practically every issue that our society faces today.
e: As the 'Central Science', chemistry is woven into the fabric of practically every issue that our society faces today. Chemistry is called the central science because it links physics to biology and to materials.

q: The usual definition is that chemistry is a study of ____ and the changes it undergoes.
e: The usual definition is that chemistry is a study of matter and the changes it undergoes. Chemistry studies matter and the changes matter undergoes.

q: What is matter? It is anything that has ____ and occupies space.
e: What is matter? It is anything that has mass and occupies space. Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space.

q: We change matter to make it more ____.
e: We change matter to make it more useful. Useful is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Some matter we change to extract a part of its energy; for example, we burn ____ to get energy to propel our automobiles.
e: Some matter we change to extract a part of its energy; for example, we burn gasoline to get energy to propel our automobiles. Gasoline is the idea that completes this fact.

q: We practice chemistry when we cook in the kitchen, when we clean our house or paint our room, when we apply ____, and when we take medicine or treat an injury.
e: We practice chemistry when we cook in the kitchen, when we clean our house or paint our room, when we apply cosmetics, and when we take medicine or treat an injury. Cosmetics is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Our body takes ____ from the air and combines it with part of the food we eat to provide us with energy for every activity we undertake.
e: Our body takes oxygen from the air and combines it with part of the food we eat to provide us with energy for every activity we undertake. Your body uses oxygen from air with food to release energy. Oxygen supports respiration and combustion, and it is a very reactive non-metal.

q: It deals with matter from the tiniest parts of ____ to the complex human body.
e: It deals with matter from the tiniest parts of atoms to the complex human body. Atoms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Prehistoric time to the beginning of Christian era (about 300 BC) is classified as ____ period.
e: Prehistoric time to the beginning of Christian era (about 300 BC) is classified as black magic period. Black magic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The ancients believed the world made of '____', which are earth, air, water and fire.
e: The ancients believed the world made of 'four elements', which are earth, air, water and fire. An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom.

q: The ____ were perhaps the first to formulate theories explaining the behaviour of matter without confirming their theories by experimentation.
e: The Greek philosophers were perhaps the first to formulate theories explaining the behaviour of matter without confirming their theories by experimentation. Greek philosophers is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Their philosophic point of view of nature, which can be attributed mainly to ____, dominated the Greek culture.
e: Their philosophic point of view of nature, which can be attributed mainly to Aristotle, dominated the Greek culture. Aristotle is the idea that completes this fact.

q: From about 300 BC to the end of 17th century, the experimental roots of chemistry are planted in ____, a mystical chemistry that flourished in China and Europe.
e: From about 300 BC to the end of 17th century, the experimental roots of chemistry are planted in alchemy, a mystical chemistry that flourished in China and Europe. Alchemy is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Alchemists made several attempts to turn cheaper metals to gold, using the substance called the ____.
e: Alchemists made several attempts to turn cheaper metals to gold, using the substance called the Philosopher's Stone. Philosopher's Stone is the idea that completes this fact.

q: They also wanted to find an ____ that would enable people to live longer and cure all ailments.
e: They also wanted to find an elixir that would enable people to live longer and cure all ailments. Elixir is the idea that completes this fact.

q: They also wanted to find an elixir that would enable people to live longer and cure all ____.
e: They also wanted to find an elixir that would enable people to live longer and cure all ailments. Ailments is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In 1661 ____ developed the basic ideas about the behaviour of gases.
e: In 1661 Robert Boyle developed the basic ideas about the behaviour of gases. Robert Boyle is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Traditional chemistry period started by the end of 17th century up to the middle of ____ century.
e: Traditional chemistry period started by the end of 17th century up to the middle of 19th century. 19th is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In 1774 ____ discovered a gas, later named oxygen.
e: In 1774 Joseph Priestley discovered a gas, later named oxygen. Priestley's 1774 work is the isolation of oxygen gas.

q: Chemistry was introduced to the science in 1768 by French chemist ____, who explained the law of conservation of matter based on the experimentation method.
e: Chemistry was introduced to the science in 1768 by French chemist Antoine Lavoisier, who explained the law of conservation of matter based on the experimentation method. Lavoisier weighed reactions carefully and stated conservation of mass.

q: From this onward, scientists use the experimentation method, also known as ____, rather than logical and theoretical method of the ancients.
e: From this onward, scientists use the experimentation method, also known as scientific method, rather than logical and theoretical method of the ancients. Scientific method is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In 1803 ____ postulated Atomic Theory, which states that all matter is composed of atoms, which are small and indivisible.
e: In 1803 John Dalton postulated Atomic Theory, which states that all matter is composed of atoms, which are small and indivisible. Dalton treated atoms as the tiny particles that make up elements.

q: ____ laid the groundwork for a more quantitative approach to chemistry by calculating the number of particles in a given amount of a gas, which we use today as Avogadro's constant.
e: Amedeo Avogadro laid the groundwork for a more quantitative approach to chemistry by calculating the number of particles in a given amount of a gas, which we use today as Avogadro's constant. Avogadro linked gas volume to the number of particles, which leads to the mole.

q: Modern chemistry starts from the middle of 19th century to the ____ time.
e: Modern chemistry starts from the middle of 19th century to the present time. Present is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Scientific facts remain the same, no matter who does the ____.
e: Scientific facts remain the same, no matter who does the measuring. Measuring is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Few of the areas that have emerged as being especially important in modern chemistry are Synthesis, Separation techniques, Identification and assay, Materials, Polymers, ____, Biochemistry, Molecular biology, Green chemistry, and Combinatorial chemistry.
e: Few of the areas that have emerged as being especially important in modern chemistry are Synthesis, Separation techniques, Identification and assay, Materials, Polymers, Nanochemistry, Biochemistry, Molecular biology, Green chemistry, and Combinatorial chemistry. Nanochemistry is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ____, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on.
e: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on. Ores is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and ____, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on.
e: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on. Glazes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and ____, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on.
e: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on. Wine is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and ____, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on.
e: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on. Plant extracts have long been used as medicine and as perfume.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into ____, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on.
e: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on. Turning fat into soap is an old chemical change, a kind of saponification.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of ____, and making of alloys like bronze and so on.
e: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on. Making glass from sand and alkali is an early industrial chemical change.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like ____ and so on.
e: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on. Bronze is an alloy, made by combining metals, so it is a chemical material.

q: Alchemists never achieved these goals, but they discovered many new chemical substances and techniques such as ____ and extraction that are still used today.
e: Alchemists never achieved these goals, but they discovered many new chemical substances and techniques such as distillation and extraction that are still used today. Distillation separates liquids by boiling point, then condenses the vapour.

q: Alchemists never achieved these goals, but they discovered many new chemical substances and techniques such as distillation and ____ that are still used today.
e: Alchemists never achieved these goals, but they discovered many new chemical substances and techniques such as distillation and extraction that are still used today. Extraction is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chemical reactions occur when you breathe, eat, or just sit there ____.
e: Chemical reactions occur when you breathe, eat, or just sit there reading. Reading is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The air you are breathing is a mixture of elements like ____ and nitrogen.
e: The air you are breathing is a mixture of elements like oxygen and nitrogen. Oxygen supports respiration and combustion, and it is a very reactive non-metal.

q: The book you are reading is made from wood pulp or ____ which has been bleached and treated with various chemicals.
e: The book you are reading is made from wood pulp or cellulose which has been bleached and treated with various chemicals. Cellulose is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The clothes you are wearing are probably made from synthetic chemicals called ____, such as nylon or terylene.
e: The clothes you are wearing are probably made from synthetic chemicals called polymers, such as nylon or terylene. Polymers is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The seat you are sitting on is perhaps a plastic polymer, with ____; foam seat padding and metal support.
e: The seat you are sitting on is perhaps a plastic polymer, with polyurethane; foam seat padding and metal support. Polyurethane is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The room you are in is made from cement, plastics, concrete and ____, all of which are chemicals.
e: The room you are in is made from cement, plastics, concrete and glass, all of which are chemicals. Making glass from sand and alkali is an early industrial chemical change.

q: Some chemicals are ____.
e: Some chemicals are toxic. Toxic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: All matter is made of chemicals, so the importance of chemistry is that it is the study of ____.
e: All matter is made of chemicals, so the importance of chemistry is that it is the study of everything. Everything is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The five main branches are considered to be Organic chemistry, Inorganic chemistry, Physical chemistry, Analytical chemistry, and ____.
e: The five main branches are considered to be Organic chemistry, Inorganic chemistry, Physical chemistry, Analytical chemistry, and Biochemistry. Biochemistry is the chemistry of living organisms and their processes.

q: In addition, Nuclear chemistry, Environmental chemistry, Industrial chemistry, Polymer chemistry, Materials chemistry, Nanochemistry, Green chemistry, Agricultural chemistry, Theoretical chemistry, etc., are other branches of ____.
e: In addition, Nuclear chemistry, Environmental chemistry, Industrial chemistry, Polymer chemistry, Materials chemistry, Nanochemistry, Green chemistry, Agricultural chemistry, Theoretical chemistry, etc., are other branches of chemistry. Chemistry is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In addition, Nuclear chemistry, ____ chemistry, Industrial chemistry, Polymer chemistry, Materials chemistry, Nanochemistry, Green chemistry, Agricultural chemistry, Theoretical chemistry, etc., are other branches of chemistry.
e: In addition, Nuclear chemistry, Environmental chemistry, Industrial chemistry, Polymer chemistry, Materials chemistry, Nanochemistry, Green chemistry, Agricultural chemistry, Theoretical chemistry, etc., are other branches of chemistry. Environmental is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In addition, Nuclear chemistry, Environmental chemistry, Industrial chemistry, Polymer chemistry, Materials chemistry, Nanochemistry, Green chemistry, ____ chemistry, Theoretical chemistry, etc., are other branches of chemistry.
e: In addition, Nuclear chemistry, Environmental chemistry, Industrial chemistry, Polymer chemistry, Materials chemistry, Nanochemistry, Green chemistry, Agricultural chemistry, Theoretical chemistry, etc., are other branches of chemistry. Agricultural is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Organic chemistry is the study of most carbon-containing chemicals which are hydrocarbons and their ____.
e: Organic chemistry is the study of most carbon-containing chemicals which are hydrocarbons and their derivatives. Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, especially hydrocarbons and their derivatives.

q: Inorganic chemistry is the study of, in general, matter that does not deal with ____.
e: Inorganic chemistry is the study of, in general, matter that does not deal with hydrocarbons. A hydrocarbon contains only hydrogen and carbon. Inorganic chemistry studies the rest of the elements and their compounds, not just hydrocarbons.

q: Physical chemistry is the study of the behaviour and changes of matter and the related ____ changes.
e: Physical chemistry is the study of the behaviour and changes of matter and the related energy changes. Energy is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Analytical chemistry is the study of components and ____ of substances.
e: Analytical chemistry is the study of components and compositions of substances. Compositions is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Biochemistry is the study of matter and processes of ____ organisms.
e: Biochemistry is the study of matter and processes of living organisms. Living is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Physical chemistry is the study of the behaviour and changes of matter and the related energy changes, such as reaction rates and reaction ____.
e: Physical chemistry is the study of the behaviour and changes of matter and the related energy changes, such as reaction rates and reaction mechanisms. Mechanisms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Analytical chemistry is the study of components and compositions of substances, including food nutrients, quality control (QC) and quality ____ (QA).
e: Analytical chemistry is the study of components and compositions of substances, including food nutrients, quality control (QC) and quality assurance (QA). Assurance is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Biochemistry is the study of matter and processes of living organisms, such as metabolism and ____.
e: Biochemistry is the study of matter and processes of living organisms, such as metabolism and fermentation. Fermentation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Inorganic chemistry is the study of, in general, matter that does not deal with hydrocarbons, such as minerals, metals and non-metals, and ____.
e: Inorganic chemistry is the study of, in general, matter that does not deal with hydrocarbons, such as minerals, metals and non-metals, and semi-conductors. Semi-conductors is the idea that completes this fact.

q: By studying and understanding chemistry, you will become a global citizen in the ____ first century.
e: By studying and understanding chemistry, you will become a global citizen in the twenty first century. Twenty is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The principles of chemistry are needed to understand the nature of every form of ____.
e: The principles of chemistry are needed to understand the nature of every form of matter. Chemistry studies matter and the changes matter undergoes.

q: For example, metals, drugs, gasoline, foods, the earth's crust, water, atmosphere, radioactive materials and the human brain cell, all have properties determined mainly by ____ principles.
e: For example, metals, drugs, gasoline, foods, the earth's crust, water, atmosphere, radioactive materials and the human brain cell, all have properties determined mainly by chemical principles. A chemical property describes how a substance reacts to make something new.

q: Consumer aspects of chemistry and the chemistry of common things can also be known from the fundamental ideas of ____.
e: Consumer aspects of chemistry and the chemistry of common things can also be known from the fundamental ideas of chemistry. Chemistry is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chemistry has helped in establishing industries which manufacture utility goods, such as acids, alkalis, soaps, ____, dyes, polymers, metals, etc.
e: Chemistry has helped in establishing industries which manufacture utility goods, such as acids, alkalis, soaps, detergents, dyes, polymers, metals, etc. Detergents is the idea that completes this fact.

q: These industries contribute in a big way to the ____ of a nation and generate employment.
e: These industries contribute in a big way to the economy of a nation and generate employment. Economy is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chemistry is also required for many fields of ____.
e: Chemistry is also required for many fields of study. Study is the idea that completes this fact.

q: For example, courses in Pharmacy and ____ require applicants to have knowledge of chemistry; cutting-edge of today's digital technology requires knowledge on the principles of chemistry.
e: For example, courses in Pharmacy and Medicine require applicants to have knowledge of chemistry; cutting-edge of today's digital technology requires knowledge on the principles of chemistry. Medicine is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chemistry is considered as an ____ science.
e: Chemistry is considered as an experimental science. Experimental is the idea that completes this fact.

q: You should recognise that the principles and laws of nature are the results of extensive observations and speculative analyses refined over many ____.
e: You should recognise that the principles and laws of nature are the results of extensive observations and speculative analyses refined over many investigations. Investigations is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Basic process skills such as observing, classifying, inferring, communicating, measuring, predicting and using numbers will be developed if you study ____.
e: Basic process skills such as observing, classifying, inferring, communicating, measuring, predicting and using numbers will be developed if you study chemistry. Chemistry is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Basic process skills such as observing, classifying, inferring, communicating (through diagram, graph, chart, etc.), measuring, predicting and using ____ will be developed if you study chemistry.
e: Basic process skills such as observing, classifying, inferring, communicating (through diagram, graph, chart, etc.), measuring, predicting and using numbers will be developed if you study chemistry. Numbers is the idea that completes this fact.

q: You are expected to enhance the development of these skills and use them to construct your chemical knowledge, and hence engage in ____ learning.
e: You are expected to enhance the development of these skills and use them to construct your chemical knowledge, and hence engage in life-long learning. Life-long is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Agriculture also uses chemistry in many areas, and it is very important for the food and beverage industry and ____ industry.
e: Agriculture also uses chemistry in many areas, and it is very important for the food and beverage industry and medical industry. Medical is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Basic chemistry is the branch of science that studies the preparation, properties, structures and ____ of material substances.
e: Basic chemistry is the branch of science that studies the preparation, properties, structures and reactions of material substances. Reactions is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Basic chemistry is the branch of science that studies the preparation, properties, structures and reactions of material ____.
e: Basic chemistry is the branch of science that studies the preparation, properties, structures and reactions of material substances. A property is physical if measuring it leaves the substance itself unchanged, and chemical if composition changes.

q: Chemistry contributes to a large extent in the development and growth of a ____.
e: Chemistry contributes to a large extent in the development and growth of a nation. Nation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A developing country, like Myanmar, needs talented and creative ____.
e: A developing country, like Myanmar, needs talented and creative chemists. Chemists is the idea that completes this fact.

q: To be a good chemist, one needs to understand the basic concepts of ____.
e: To be a good chemist, one needs to understand the basic concepts of chemistry. Chemistry is the idea that completes this fact.

q: On this context, there are six main themes in Basic Education High School Chemistry Course: Particulate nature of substances, Periodicity, Chemical calculations, Chemistry of reactions, the Environment and ____ chemistry.
e: On this context, there are six main themes in Basic Education High School Chemistry Course: Particulate nature of substances, Periodicity, Chemical calculations, Chemistry of reactions, the Environment and Organic chemistry. Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, especially hydrocarbons and their derivatives.

q: Knowledge of these chemistry principles will help you to better understand the ____ and hazards to mankind and enable you to make intelligent decisions in the future.
e: Knowledge of these chemistry principles will help you to better understand the benefits and hazards to mankind and enable you to make intelligent decisions in the future. Benefits is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Knowledge of these chemistry principles will help you to better understand the benefits and hazards to mankind and enable you to make intelligent decisions in the ____.
e: Knowledge of these chemistry principles will help you to better understand the benefits and hazards to mankind and enable you to make intelligent decisions in the future. Future is the idea that completes this fact.
